boundary_and_context_notes.reading: Mishnah: general rule and three named alternatives; retain conditions and direction of intention.
Closed local explanation of אלא, persistent sanctity, Rava’s blood rule, and two grounds.

New Ravina report to Rav Pappa of Rava’s challenge/resolution: unmarked sacrifices stand for their designated purpose, whereas a woman does not stand for divorce. Do not attribute Rava’s arguments to Ravina or Rav Pappa.
Attempts to substantiate default sacrificial intent culminate in Rabbi Yose’s court-condition teaching; earlier proofs are challenged, not retained as conclusive.

Separate proof chain for unmarked divorce documents includes rejected candidates and concludes with Rav Yehuda reporting Shmuel about leaving the formula blank. Read to3a:8 to establish transition to another contradiction; no producer context consulted.

ambiguity_and_omission_risks: Distinguish offering validity from discharge of the owner’s obligation.
The Passover exception is time-conditioned; the sin and Rabbi Eliezer guilt exceptions apply at every time.
Yose ben Honi concerns other offerings slaughtered FOR Passover/sin designations; do not reverse the direction into the first tanna’s exception.
Shimon’s higher/lower rule requires keeping actual and intended classes ordered; כשר does not itself settle whether obligation is discharged.
Do not treat the absence of an explicit time condition in Yose’s words as an adjudication of every possible time condition elsewhere in the tractate.
The vow/freewill derivation crosses 2a:10–2b:1 and needs the rhetorical prohibition in2b:2 to support Rava.
Rational and scriptural grounds are alternatives; no different named speakers are asserted.
Mishnah and Gemara boundary falls at2a:6 with preserved markup.
Context evidence is not counted as endpoint-core claim extraction.
